messages:
Maria (runtime): starting a low-traffic canary for release v2.6.3 now, routing 5% to canary pool. Will watch p50/p95/p99 for the next 15m :eyes:
OpsBot: deploy initiated by Maria at 2026-03-17T12:03:32Z, canary fraction=5%, nodes=[canary-1..3] :white_check_mark:
Maria (runtime): quick heads-up — p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~800-1200ms for long-seq requests after ~4m. Not visible on p50.
Ajay: I see the spike in the dashboard too. Appears correlated with seq_len>1024 requests. Can someone grab a pprof or flamegraph from canary-2? :warning:
Tim: on it. Can someone confirm which tag is running on canary-2?
Maria (runtime): canary-2 is running image redwood/runtime:v2.6.3-rc3 (tag sha: c3f9d8).
Len (perf): I can run a lightweight perf on canary-2. Need the repro load command and a short window. Prefer to start off sampling on inference worker threads only.
Ajay: repro: run this locally against canary internal DNS: `ab -n 200 -c 5 http://canary-2.internal/redwood/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":2048}'`
Len (perf): ok running `perf record -g -F 99 -p $(pidof runtime_worker)` for 30s. Will upload flamegraph when done.
Sophia: quick thought — we enabled an experimental kv-cache TTL tweak in this rollout. Could be invalidation thrash for long sequences. Any logs about cache evictions?
Tim: grabbing eviction stats: `curl http://canary-2.internal/metrics | grep kv_cache_evictions` -> shows a spike matching the p99 window. Sending metric snapshot.
Maria (runtime): thanks. Given eviction spike + flamegraph request, let's hold scaled rollout. Don't increase traffic beyond 5% until we confirm. :no_entry_sign:
DeployBot: hold applied to v2.6.3 canary rollout by Maria. Traffic frozen at 5%.
Len (perf): flamegraph attached (uploaded to #perf-artifacts). Early look: 45% of samples in softmax kernel and a surprising chunk in buffer compact routine. Not purely kernel-level, looks like memory copies while handling long KV chains.
Ajay: that maps to the kv-cache TTL theory. If the cache is invalidating more, worker does more recompute and memcopy for large seqs. Could be a GC or allocator interaction on the new runtime.
Sophia: I can roll back the TTL tweak in a build and push a patch to canary-2. How fast can we get a patched image?
Maria (runtime): if patch is small we can build and push in ~25m. Meanwhile, do we need a partial rollback plan? If this is just a config toggle we can flip it via feature flag.
Tim: config flip would be fastest. I can flip the TTL back to previous value for canary pool, but need access to the feature-flag manager. Who has perms?
Ajay: I can do the flag flip. Planning to set kv_cache_ttl=3600 -> 0 (previous) for canary nodes. Will monitor p99 after change.
Len (perf): still uploading full flamegraph. Will also run `heaptrack` if p99 doesn't drop after config revert.
Ajay: repro: flipping kv_cache_ttl to 0 now. Patch: `/api/flags/set?kv_cache_ttl=0&scope=canary` -> 200 OK.
Maria (runtime): thanks. Keeping monitoring window open for 10m.
OpsBot: metric alert suppressed for canary p99 during investigation (alert id: a-3198).
Tim: initial read — p99 dropped to ~140ms after the flip. Looks promising.
Sophia: great. If this holds for 15m we can either continue rollout with a guard or ship the config revert to main. My preference: revert the TTL tweak in the backend code and re-evaluate the optimization in a lab environment.
Maria (runtime): agree. Action items: (1) Ajay confirm flag flip stable for 15m, (2) Sophia create revert PR and link to this thread, (3) Len follow-up with heaptrack if variance persists, (4) Tim update release checklist to include kv-cache TTL in canary checks.
Ajay: will keep an eye for 30m. Pager window open; I'll escalate if p99 rises again. :thumbsup:
Len (perf): flamegraph + perf logs uploaded. Starting heaptrack only if we see regression recurring.
DeployBot: canary hold still in effect. To proceed with ramp we need: p99 within baseline for 30m and no new evictions.
Maria (runtime): closing loop — thanks all. Reopen thread if anything regresses.
Tim: PR from Sophia linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427 — includes unit tests and a revert of the TTL tweak.
Sophia: PR ready for review, tagging @Maria (runtime) @Tim @Len (perf).
Maria (runtime): will review and approve once we confirm 30m stability. Great job coordinating. :tada:
